card.title: You Owe Me a Miracle
card.instruction: Carry one past favor as sufficient reason to expect an impossible act in return, and present the exchange as perfectly fair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I covered your lunch yesterday. Bring back the ten minutes I spent queuing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That covers the sandwich. I'm only asking for my time back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can queue for you today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then join yesterday's queue ahead of me. Hand me the sandwich before I waste ten minutes. That settles both parts.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands lost queue time for the lunch favor, A3 separates food from time, and A5 makes B's queue offer retroactive so both components are supposedly repaid.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's lunch offer causes A3's two-part accounting; B4's queue offer causes A5's specific instruction to enter yesterday's line ahead of A.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 offer concrete normal reciprocity, which A treats as incomplete rather than irrelevant.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's exact proposed service to specify an impossible intervention before the original wait.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes yesterday's lunch and ten-minute queue; A5 keeps the same sandwich and lost interval.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's settles-both-parts close is earned by A3's food-time distinction and B4's queue service.
